study: Feasibility gate Phase 1: concepts against ISS-022 (T00)

E.what: axisymmetric coil behind the shield, in its shadow
E.verdict: NARROWS, DOES NOT REMOVE: the leak area falls with the extra field, but the forward pole stays a field zero, so the shield centre still takes the full free-expansion fluence inside a smaller spot. It only shrinks a sacrificial insert.

A1.what: C1 and C2 tilted together about the burn point in the x-z plane (conductor, currents and stand-off unchanged)

A2.what: circular coil, axis across the nozzle axis, behind the shield inside its X-ray shadow

B.what: inert forward cap on the target (forward-suppressing target), momentum sharing only
conflicts: the 9 driver beams arrive from polar 3.5-4 deg and the fast ignitor from 1-2 deg: a forward cap sits in their path, so it is part of the target physics (T04 class), not an add-on
momentum sharing is an upper bound on the benefit: a hot cap re-expands and part of its energy comes back as radiation
the debris still flies along the field zero and lands on the shield centre, slower but as condensable mass

C.what: two nozzles splayed about the ship axis (alternate burn-point arrangement)
costs: two coil sets, two shields, two driver/injector sets (each at half power, the coil mass per pulse energy is unchanged, so total coil mass roughly x2 at the same pulse energy, or x2^(1/3)..x1 with smaller pulses)
each burn point now sees the ship from the side: the X-ray and neutron shadow geometry (FDP-1 Omega 0.025) is rebuilt
a single nozzle cannot be canted: its thrust must pass through the centre of mass, and its forward channel lies on that line
C.verdict: GEOMETRICALLY POSSIBLE, NOT EVALUATED AS A SHIP: it is a different propulsion architecture (two Fiji nozzles), outside this gate; kept as an open lane.

S.what: sacrificial or renewable shield-centre insert inside the leak spot
S.verdict: NOT VIABLE: the spot takes about 340 J/cm2 per pulse (about 650 MW/m2 average); a solid face would ablate tens of microns per pulse (metres per hour), and a renewable lithium face would consume lithium at plug-like rates. The fluence must fall by about 198x before any permanent face survives.

chosen.concept: A1: C1 and C2 tilted 14 deg as a rigid pair, whole nozzle turned 2.7 deg so the thrust passes through the centre of mass
chosen.status: ANALYTICALLY PROMISING (vacuum-field thin shell); NOT a demonstrated plasma solution
chosen.booked_note: no added conductor; the pulsed side load and the re-placed C1/C2 supports are inside the coil strut booking (PROTOTYPE); the thrust loss is booked as a nozzle-efficiency factor
